svg.text: NAVAL NEWS TECHNICAL CASE STUDY // TACTICAL ARCHITECTURE
THE PERSIAN GULF 300-SECOND DILEMMA: ASYMMETRIC SWARM AMBUSH & UWE COUNTER-MEASURES
1. TACTICAL ENGAGEMENT GEOMETRY // 4.0 NM RADAR-BREAKOUT AMBUSH
2. DOCTRINAL PARADOX // CONVENTIONAL VS UWE COUNTER-SWARM
Scramble transit from Al Udeid / Diego Garcia takes 25–35 min. Ambush ends in 5 min.
5-inch gun max 16 rpm (1 target/min). Phalanx CIWS dual-mounts empty ammo in 20s.
Firing $2M–$4M ESSM/SM-2 against $50k craft exhausts magazines in 180s.
UWE SOLUTION: IN-SITU EDGE CYBER-PHYSICAL SHIELD
Two 30mm Bushmaster USVs fire 435 ABM rounds; neutralize 38 hostile hulls in 180s.
Airburst penetrations ignite 500kg RDX warheads; shockwaves swamp adjacent wingmen.
Engagement resolved at 1,200m standoff—far outside 250m blast / 600m frag limits.
Reserve USV steps into screen; battle logged to mesh ledger before alert reaches HQ.
3. UWE 6-PHASE AUTONOMOUS COUNTER-SWARM EXECUTION SEQUENCE // SECOND-BY-SECOND OODA LOOP

g.text: • Forward USV pickets detect radar & IR breakout surge
• Edge-AI models filter thermal inversions & water glint
• Rejects false-positive dhows; classifies 38 military hulls
• Dynamic threat weighting: collision vectors = Wmax
• Solves real-time bipartite matching for firing sectors
• Allocates 2 forward USVs (800 rd capacity vs 450 need)
• Strict reserve rule: 1 USV held 800m rear for leakers
• 4 UCV aerial multirotors launched for overhead paint
• USVs sprint at 48–52 kts via tunnel waterjets (P: J)
• Lateral geometry sprint avoids inefficient tail-chase
• Locks 1,200m standoff crossfire perimeter at gates
• Hits 500kg bow warheads; high-order blast propagation
• Overhead UCVs confirm zero surface radar contacts
• Logs ammo expenditure & telemetry to mesh ledger
• Reserve USV steps up; screen fully reset in 50s
